name: Port Perry Food Bank
address: 225 Water St, Port Perry, ON
description: The township's primary food bank, run by volunteers from several local faith communities. No referral needed. Serves all of Scugog Township including Blackstock, Caesarea, and Nestleton.

name: Scugog Community Harvest Table
address: Community Centre, 181 Perry St, Port Perry, ON
description: Local farmers and gardeners donate surplus seasonal produce twice monthly. Take what you need. A quiet, unhurried way to connect with where your food comes from.

name: Durham Community Legal Clinic
address: Scugog outreach — call ahead for location
description: Free legal aid for low-income residents: tenant rights, lease disputes, eviction notices, and social assistance appeals. Staff travel to Scugog monthly. Spanish interpretation available on request.

name: Scugog Shores Tenant Network
address: Meets at Scugog Memorial Library
description: Informal peer support group for renters navigating Scugog's tightening rental market. Know-your-rights resources, shared landlord experiences, and connections to formal legal supports when needed.

name: Port Perry Waterfront Park
address: Lakeshore Drive at Queen St, Port Perry, ON
description: A wide, accessible lakefront park on Lake Scugog with benches, picnic tables, a gazebo, and a community bulletin board. Used year-round — packed in summer, quietly beautiful in winter. One of the few genuinely public gathering spaces in the township.

name: Scugog Memorial Public Library
address: 231 Water St, Port Perry, ON
description: Free wifi, printing, notary service, and meeting rooms bookable at no charge. Librarians here are genuinely helpful — they will assist with government forms, job applications, and anything else you are uncertain about.

name: Port Perry Repair Café
address: Scugog Shores Museum, 16210 Island Rd, Port Perry, ON
description: Volunteer repair technicians fix small appliances, clothing, jewellery, and electronics for free. Bring what is broken. Watch it being repaired so you can do it yourself next time. No charge — donations welcome.

name: Doug's Small Engine Repair (Community Help)
address: Blackstock area — call first
description: Doug has been fixing lawnmowers, outboard motors, and farm equipment for 35 years. He helps neighbours at cost or trade. If you are a senior or on a fixed income, he often will not charge at all. Ask around in Blackstock.
contact: Word of mouth — ask at Blackstock General Store

name: Scugog Fibre Arts Collective
address: Rotating homes and the Legion hall
description: A group of knitters, weavers, and hand-sewers who meet weekly. Beginners welcome. Surplus yarn and fabric available free. They have collectively made blankets for the shelter, hats for the food bank, and anything else the community needs.

name: Lake Scugog Growers Collective
address: Port Perry Farmers Market, 178 Queen St
description: Eight local farms selling vegetables, eggs, honey, preserves, and cut flowers at the weekly market. Several accept EBT and SNAP. Ask the collective booth about their winter box program.

name: Royal Canadian Legion Branch 419
address: 65 Simcoe St, Port Perry, ON
description: The Legion hall is genuinely open to the community — not just veterans. Hall rentals are cheap, the bar is the most affordable in town, and it is one of the few places where different generations of Scugog residents actually mix. The meeting room is available free to community groups.

name: Caesarea Community Hall
address: 2nd Line, Caesarea, ON
description: Small but functional community hall in Caesarea on the northeast shore of Lake Scugog. Used for church suppers, 4-H meetings, and neighbourhood gatherings. An important anchor for the rural north end of the township.

name: Scugog Mutual Aid Network
address: Mobile — coordinated via Facebook group
description: Neighbours helping neighbours with rides to medical appointments in Oshawa or Toronto, emergency groceries, firewood, and winter wellness checks. Especially active in the rural parts of the township where isolation is a real problem.

name: Scugog Fuel and Heating Bank
address: Coordinated through local churches — call first
description: Emergency heating fuel assistance for residents who run out before the end of winter. A coalition of local churches administers this quietly and without bureaucracy. One call is usually enough.

name: Durham Farm Connections Co-op
address: Operates across Durham Region including Scugog
description: A cooperative connecting small farms with buyers, CSA subscribers, and food businesses across Durham Region. Scugog farmers make up a significant portion of the membership. Open to new farm and community members.

name: Port Perry Tool & Equipment Library
address: c/o Scugog Memorial Library, 231 Water St
description: A small but growing borrowing library of tools, garden equipment, and home repair gear. Currently 60 items and expanding. Run by volunteers. Membership is $30/year or two volunteer shifts. Started by three neighbours in 2023.

name: Scugog Arts Community Studio
address: 145 Queen St, Port Perry, ON
description: Cooperative studio and gallery run by local artists. Regular open workshops in painting, printmaking, and ceramics. Pay-what-you-can sessions on the first Tuesday of each month.

name: Nestleton Community Garden
address: Near Nestleton Station, Concession 9
description: Six-plot community garden in the rural south of the township. Plots are free but waitlisted. Surplus from common areas is available to anyone. A rare piece of shared growing space in an area with no public transit.

name: Free Little Library Network — Scugog
address: Multiple locations across Port Perry
description: Over a dozen free little libraries across Port Perry and the rural township, including several with seed envelopes in spring. The one at Scugog Shores Museum has a dedicated children's section and a small collection on local and Indigenous history.

name: Scugog Women's Resource Centre
address: Call for location — Port Perry area
description: Confidential support, crisis counselling, and practical assistance for women and families in Scugog. Helps navigate housing, legal, and financial systems. One of the most quietly essential services in the township.

name: Port Perry Horticultural Society
address: Monthly meetings at Port Perry Legion
description: One of the oldest continuous community organizations in the township. Monthly talks, seed swaps, garden tours, and a very good plant sale in May. Genuinely intergenerational — newcoming residents find community here quickly.

name: Scugog Land Back & Stewardship Circle
address: Meets at Scugog Shores Museum and on the land
hours: Seasonal gatherings — subscribe to mailing list
description: A small but growing circle of Indigenous and settler residents working on land stewardship, treaty education, and the long-term question of land access and food sovereignty in Scugog Township, which sits on Mississauga Anishinaabe territory.

name: Blackstock General Store
address: Main St, Blackstock, ON
description: The social centre of Blackstock, full stop. The bulletin board here is the most reliable information source for the south end of the township. If you want to know what is happening, who needs help, or who is selling firewood — come here.

name: Scugog Community Composting Station
address: Municipal Yard, 181 Perry St, Port Perry, ON
hours: Year-round — check Township website for hours
description: Drop off kitchen and garden waste. Finished compost is available free to Scugog residents in spring — fill as many bags as you can carry. One of the township's better-kept secrets.

name: Repair It Forward — Scugog
address: Various — check Facebook for next location
description: A newer initiative bringing bike repair, appliance fixing, and clothing mending to different corners of the township each quarter. Deliberately moves between Port Perry, Blackstock, and Caesarea so rural residents don't have to drive.

name: Durham East Cross Forest Conservation Area
address: 4560 Devitts Rd, Blackstock, ON (east of Regional Rd 57)
description: A forested conservation area south of Blackstock with trail access through mixed woodland. Maintained by the Central Lake Ontario Conservation Authority. One of the larger natural areas in the south end of the township.
contact: Explore Durham East Cross Forest | Trails and Nature

name: Scugog Island Crown Land
address: Island Road, north of Great Blue Heron Casino, Port Perry, ON
hours: Open year-round — check Crown Land Use Policy Atlas for permitted uses
description: Publicly accessible Crown land on Scugog Island. Follow Island Road north past the Great Blue Heron Charity Casino to the Carnegie Beach Road intersection — a marked entrance will be on your right. Used for walking, birdwatching, and quiet recreation.
contact: Crown Land Use Policy Atlas | ontario.ca

name: Nonquon Provincial Wildlife Area
address: Access from Scugog Line 10, Old Simcoe Road, and Scugog Line 12
description: A provincially significant wildlife area known for waterfowl, amphibians, and wetland habitat. Multiple access points off Scugog Lines 10 and 12. No facilities — come for the birds, the quiet, and the seasonal flooding spectacle.

name: Crow's Pass Conservation Area
address: 231 Middle March Rd, Port Perry, ON
description: A quiet conservation area south of Port Perry with forested trails, wetlands, and creek corridors. Maintained by CLOCA. Good for a short walk without needing to leave the township.
contact: Crow's Pass | CLOCA | Central Lake Ontario Conservation Authority

name: Beaver River Wetland Conservation Area
address: Beaver River Wetland, Lake Simcoe Region
description: A significant wetland conservation area at the northern edge of Scugog's watershed, managed by the Lake Simcoe Region Conservation Authority. Important habitat for migratory birds and rare plant species.
contact: Beaver River Wetland — Lake Simcoe Region Conservation Authority
